title: Data Types
objectives: Tell integer, decimal, text, and boolean data types apart
Pick the right data type for a value

hook.text: "20", "20.5", and "twenty": all three look like they are about numbers, but to a computer they are completely different things.

concept.heading: Four basic types
concept.body: Integer (5, -3, 100): numbers with no decimal part. Decimal (3.14, 0.5): numbers with a fractional part. Text ("Ali", "hello"): sequences of characters, written inside quotes. Boolean (TRUE / FALSE): can only take two values.

concept.heading: Why does it matter?
concept.body: A variable's type decides what you can do with it. You cannot add two pieces of text, but you can add two integers. Choosing the wrong type makes your algorithm fail.

exercises.question: What data type is the value "17"?

feedback.correct: Correct. A number with no decimal part: an integer.
feedback.incorrect: 17 has no decimal part, so it is an integer.

exercises.question: What data type is the value "3.14"?

feedback.correct: Correct. A number with a fractional part: decimal.
feedback.incorrect: 3.14 has a fractional part, so its type is decimal.

exercises.question: What data type is the value "Hello world"?

feedback.correct: Correct. A sequence of characters: text.
feedback.incorrect: Expressions made of characters are text (string) values.

exercises.question: Which type is best for storing the answer to "Did the student pass the exam?"

feedback.correct: Correct. The boolean type is ideal for information that can only be TRUE or FALSE.
feedback.incorrect: This question has only two possible answers (yes or no), so the boolean type fits best.

exercises.question: Complete the sentence.
exercises.template: If the name "Ahmet" is stored in a variable, the variable's type must be ___.

exercises.question: Which type is best for storing the number of students in a class?

feedback.correct: Correct. A head count is always a whole number, so no decimal is needed.
feedback.incorrect: A head count cannot have a fraction (there is no such thing as 12.5 students), so an integer is used.

summary: Four basic types: integer, decimal, text, boolean.
A variable's type decides what operations you can do with it.
Use the boolean type for two-state information (yes or no).
